steps.content: The fallen creatures lie strewn across the ground in a tangled heap. They don't vanish on the spot. Instead, like poorly made clay figurines, they slowly cave in on themselves, blackening and blistering, until nothing remains but an unidentifiable puddle of residue.
EMP reaches out and prods it a couple of times. Nothing happens.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: These things... they're definitely not our usual Mania monsters.
They display a basic level of aggression... and yet, they're nothing like the creatures from before, the kind that would gleefully tear any living thing to shreds.
It's almost as if someone deliberately reshaped them into something less lethal, but infinitely more annoying.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: S-sorry! This is all my fault!
Just as you're about to pursue that line of thought, a timid, faltering apology sounds from behind you. You turn to find Murphy standing there, shifting awkwardly in place.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: It's gotta be my bad luck that caused all this! These monsters have to be because of my ability too...

steps.speaker: EMP
steps.content: Hey, stop, stop! Don't say that. Us Sinners don't get affected by luck that easily—Ow!
Before she can finish her sentence, her foot lands on a patch of melted slime, and she goes down hard, face-first into the dirt. While EMP flails on the ground, Letta steps forward from the side.

steps.speaker: Letta
steps.content: Chief didn't do anything to you, so heh... that makes you a <color=#fb9259>friend</color>.
You open your mouth to object, but it dies there as you notice Murphy, at your side, her eyes kindling with an unexpected gleam.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: F-friend!? Really!
But her excitement barely lasts a few seconds before she sinks back into her slump.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Are you sure you wanna be friends with someone like me? Every time I go outside it starts raining, food gets stuck in my teeth when I eat... even stray dogs cross the street to avoid me! What if I end up attracting more monsters...

steps.speaker: Whitestone Industries? Sure! I have so much to say about my company. Um...
steps.content: This is a Mania field. The monsters appear because of Mania.

steps.speaker: EMP
steps.content: ...Ahem! Yeah, what she said! That just now was a pure coincidence. Pure coincidence!
EMP rubs her battered backside and starts acting tough, insisting she's fine. Meanwhile, you notice an unfamiliar face standing beside her.
The woman emerges from behind EMP with unhurried ease. Even after the chaos of the battle just now, not a single speck of dust mars her coat.
I'm <color=#fb9259>Norma</color>. Forensic analyst, Public Security Bureau.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...And why is the Public Security Bureau here?

steps.speaker: Letta
steps.content: See? I told you Chief would ask the same thing!

steps.speaker: EMP
steps.content: Hey, Lantern Girl, how about a little concern over here?! Shouldn't you be asking how we even got here in the first place?!

steps.speaker: Letta
steps.content: Because that question's boring. It's like listening to your Syndicate stories. Fun the first time, but after a while, I'd rather hear something new.

Typical EMP, as she can strike up a conversation with just about anyone. Contrast that with Letta, who's practically bouncing on her heels, seemingly unbothered by the situation. If anything... she looks almost excited.

steps.speaker: Norma
steps.content: I was deployed to MBCC as support staff for data analysis. During routine information gathering, an environmental anomaly occurred.

steps.speaker: Norma
steps.content: Five minutes ago, the monitoring models I set up inside the Bureau detected a sudden shift. M-values breached critical threshold instantly and are continuing to rise.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Wait, inside the Bureau? Are you sure?
Could that crash have dragged everyone from the Bureau into this place? You suck in a sharp breath and turn, your gaze landing on Murphy, who stands sheepishly at the back of the crowd.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Uh... Chief, I couldn't have caused something this big, could I? I mean, my luck's bad, sure... but surely it wouldn't drag everyone else down with me... right?
...After seeing what Murphy's ability can do firsthand, you can't help but feel this outcome is entirely within the realm of possibility.

steps.speaker: Norma
steps.content: However, this situation was not caused by any individual. Every Sinner who came into contact with Mania has been pulled into this space.
Well, at least it's not the worst-case scenario. Ordinary people getting dragged into Mania would be a lot more trouble.
Thankfully, you had assigned the majority of your Sinners to field missions the day before. Only a handful remained inside the Bureau.
The analyzer lets out a warning ping. Norma glances down, her brow furrowing—barely, but it's there.
Within seconds, the waveform on the screen registers two spikes so close together they nearly overlap, and the source is nearby. She pauses for a moment, then quietly stows the terminal away.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Any environmental changes outside the Bureau?

steps.speaker: Norma
steps.content: Environmental data analysis is still in progress. What I can confirm for now: the Mania spread remains small-scale. Additionally, the Sinners' abilities have... <color=#fb9259>deviated</color>, to varying degrees.

steps.speaker: Norma
steps.content: As you can see, every Sinner's ability has been altered to some degree. The changes could range from negligible to drastic.

steps.speaker: Norma
steps.content: Case in point: these three.

steps.speaker: EMP
steps.content: Ohhh, so that's what's going on. I was just in my room playing games, zoned out for like a second, and boom. This happened.

steps.speaker: EMP
steps.content: Guess I'm a real Archer Queen now. Can't shake this thing off no matter what I do.
EMP gives her hand a vigorous shake, but the bow stays firmly glued to her palm; she can't fling it off no matter how hard she tries. It might as well be a slingshot fused to her arm.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Ah... Are you okay? Does it hurt? That looks like it hurts way worse than that time I accidentally super-glued my hand fixing the door handle...

steps.speaker: EMP
steps.content: Nah, it's fine. Just gotta get used to it. The lantern girl's got it worse than me.
Letta, on the other hand, is missing her ever-present lantern. It has vanished without a trace.

steps.speaker: Letta
steps.content: Hmm... The lantern's gone. It used to come right back whenever I called it, no matter where I left it.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: I totally get that... Losing something you've had for so long...

Letta now wields an enormous lamppost, ripped from who-knows-where. Her original lantern is long gone; all that remains is the sturdiest chunk of the lamppost, slung over her shoulder like a makeshift bludgeon.

steps.speaker: Letta
steps.content: Not a big deal, though. This works fine. And... I actually kinda like it.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Well... that does look way more powerful than a lantern...

It seems the deviation Norma mentioned extends over an alarmingly wide area. Everything tied to Mania has been warped by its influence. That would explain why the creatures from earlier were so weakened—the deviation is to thank for that.
So... the question now is, how do you get out of here? Or more precisely, how do you undo whatever this deviation has done to the Sinners?

steps.speaker: Letta
steps.content: Oh, and you should call me Lamppost Girl now.

steps.speaker: EMP
steps.content: Huh?! No way. Even though Hella turned into whatever she'd turn into, I'd still call her a Syndicate grey rat!

steps.speaker: EMP
steps.content: Oh yeah... speaking of Hella, you think the others from the Bureau got pulled in too? If we track them down, we might actually figure out what's going on!

options: Sounds like we're on the same page.

steps.speaker: Norma
steps.content: Theoretically, yes.

steps.speaker: EMP
steps.content: Then what're we waiting for? Let's move!
It seems even EMP can be reliable once in a while. Beside her, Murphy clenches her fists, looking ready to spring into action at any moment.

steps.speaker: Norma
steps.content: All right. You all go ahead.

steps.speaker: EMP
steps.content: Hey, hold up... What do you mean? You're not coming? And you still haven't told us what happened to your ability from the deviation!
Halfway through her step, EMP yanks her foot back.

steps.speaker: Norma
steps.content: <color=#fb9259>My ability did not deviate.</color>

steps.speaker: Everyone
steps.content: ...Huh?

steps.speaker: EMP
steps.content: So you were over there analyzing everything all serious, and the whole time nothing even happened to you?! No fair! I thought we were all in this mess together...

steps.speaker: Letta
steps.content: Actually... she's more like the family member keeping the patients company. She's just here to make us feel better.

steps.speaker: EMP
steps.content: That makes it sound even weirder!

steps.speaker: Norma
steps.content: Jokes aside. I need to return to the monitoring points I set up earlier and continue calibrating the models to pinpoint the source of the anomaly. I won't be accompanying you.
As she speaks, she pulls out a palm-sized terminal from her case, its casing still winking with indicator lights along the edges.

steps.speaker: Norma
steps.content: I'm leaving this portable analyzer with you. It will continuously monitor nearby Mania fluctuations. If you approach the anomaly source, or if it picks up any signals left by Bureau members, it will alert you.

steps.speaker: Norma
steps.content: Naturally. This is the most efficient approach. Once I've gathered sufficient data, I'll rendezvous with you.
Seeing that Norma's mind is already made up, you can only nod and accept the analyzer she hands you. Right now, information is what you need most.
Stay safe out there. Let's move.
The Sinners spring into action at once, all except Murphy, who remains frozen in place.

options: What are you spacing out for? You're gonna fall behind.

steps.content: A flicker of surprise crosses Murphy's face; the last thing she expected was being told to follow.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Wait for me!
She'd always believed that trouble, when it came, followed her like a curse—that people near her would either suffer for it or, at minimum, look at her with thinly veiled disdain.

But these people before her barely seem to register it. The monsters are bizarre, the world is bizarre, their own states are absurdly strange, and still they go about business as usual, cracking jokes on the side.
As if all of this is just <color=#fb9259>everyday life</color> to them.
...Maybe this time things could be different? Clinging to that thought, Murphy scrambles to your side.
And no one notices that in the lingering dark at the far end of the passage, something silently opens its eyes.
